verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser has a first-party pricing doc that bills usage in credits bought by subscription or direct purchase. Community comments confirm a public pricing page that lists concurrency and data-transfer allowances, which one user compared favorably to Browserbase. However, the credit model is indirect rather than a clear per-task or per-browser-hour price, and one user found it confusing to map credits to real workload cost. missing for 10: explicit per-browser-hour or per-task rates in the evidence, documented API rate limits, first-party docs on concurrency limits per plan, a clear credit-to-usage conversion.
